title: How Far Could Nvidia Stock Fall if Jensen Huang Resigns?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate sizes the worst case for Nvidia after the Jensen Huang scandal deepened. Over the weekend it emerged Huang had an affair with Alice Wang, whom the US government reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset, with ties dating to at least 2023; The Information reported her firm may have helped facilitate at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chips reaching Chinese companies. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries wants answers, the FBI is looking into it, and President Trump sounded supportive of Huang. Parkevtate says the worst case is Huang stepping down or being fired: he is irreplaceable, with no clear successor and no CEO transition training comparable to Procter & Gamble. He puts the downside at 20-30%, citing Dan Ives, though closer to 20-25% in his own view. Even so, he argues the risk is priced in: the stock is already about $70 off its $243 high, trades at a 10.5x forward P/E, the cheapest in years, with demand soaring and product sold out through next year. His DCF fair value is $312 against a ~$169 price, about 85% upside, and he says the risk-reward would still be worthwhile even at $200. Other risks stack up too: hyperscalers building their own chips, circular financing, and AI-bubble worries. He is holding and interested in adding more ahead of Q3 earnings on 17 November. Call: NVDA BUY reiterated at ~$169, fair value $312.
